headword: {呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}

definitions.gloss: enemies in the same boat; rivals cooperating
definitions.explanation: Bitter enemies or rivals who are forced to work together toward a common goal; adversaries who must cooperate due to circumstances.

examples.japanese: ⟦{政治|せいじ}→政治：01629_seiji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: In politics, enemies working together is common.

examples.japanese: ⟦{利害|りがい}→利害：04091_rigai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一致|いっち}→一致：01733_icchi⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧、{呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{協力|きょうりょく}→協力：00261_kyouryoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Because our interests aligned, we ended up cooperating despite being rivals.

examples.japanese: ⟦{競合|きょうごう}→競合：05082_kyougou⟧⟦{会社|がいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦プロジェクト→プロジェクト：06764_purojekuto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{進|すす}める→進める：01949_susumeru⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: We ended up working on the project with our rival company.

notes:
ORIGIN: This idiom comes from the ancient Chinese military text 『{孫子|そんし}』 (The Art of War). The states of {呉|ご} (Wu) and {越|えつ} (Yue) were bitter enemies, but if people from both states were on the same boat during a storm, they would have to cooperate to survive.

STRUCTURE: {呉|ご} (Wu state) + {越|えつ} (Yue state) + ⟦{同|どう}→同〜：03962_dou⟧ (same) + {舟|しゅう} (boat)

USAGE: Used to describe situations where rivals or enemies must set aside their differences and work together. Common in business, politics, and sports contexts.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{協力|きょうりょく}→協力：00261_kyouryoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to cooperate despite being rivals)
- {呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧ (a relationship of rivals forced to cooperate)
